newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greek Cypriots fire warning shots at strangers.
newsitem.headline: Greek Cypriots fire warning shots at strangers.

text.p: A Greek Cypriot sentry fired warning shots when strangers approached his post close to a mixed community village of Greek and Turkish Cypriots in Cyprus on Sunday night, the Cypriot Defence Ministry said on Monday.
The ministry said the sentry fired a round of shots after seeing persons approaching his post, west of the village of Pyla close to midnight on Sunday.
Nobody was reported injured in the incident. "The sentry said he saw suspicious movements... the incident is being investigated," a ministry spokesman told Reuters.
Pyla, in the southern Larnaca district, is in a United Nations-controlled buffer zone where some 800 Greek Cypriots and 400 Turkish Cypriots live.
"We are aware of the incident and have sought explanations from the national guard," said Waldemar Rokoszewski, a spokesman for the peacekeeping force on the island.

Tension has risen perceptibly on the eastern Mediterranean island in the past month. In August two Greek Cypriot protestors were killed by people on the Turkish Cypriot side of the island in separate incidents along the U.N.-controlled buffer zone.
Last week a Turkish Cypriot sentry was found shot dead at his post close to the ceasefire line, and another injured.
Turkish Cypriots have blamed Greek Cypriots for the killing, but the Cyprus government has denied any involvement.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey occupied its northern part in 1974 following a coup engineered by the military government then ruling Greece.
Only Turkey recognises the Turkish Cypriot breakaway state formed in 1983. The dispute is a constant source of tension between NATO allies Turkey and Greece.
